# What this run is

A **test of the full per-donor → joint isoLASER pipeline** on chr21, using the
0 hr library. The point was to establish that the chain runs correctly and to
measure the event yield at per-donor depth before committing to a genome-wide
run — not to produce biological results.

Why per donor at all: isoLASER's phasing assumes **one diploid genome**
(weighted k-means, K = 2). Run on the pooled BAM it splits *donors* rather than
haplotypes — we
[demonstrated that directly](data_summary.html), so the pooled cis/trans calls
were uninterpretable. Splitting first makes each donor's haplotype table valid;
`isolaser_joint` then pools those tables across donors.

Scripts: `3.isolaser_per_donor/` — `1.split_bam_by_donor.sbatch`,
`2.run_isolaser_per_donor.sbatch` (SLURM array), `3.run_isolaser_joint.sbatch`.
All three completed.

# Splitting the BAM

The cell barcode is in the `RG` tag, so `samtools view -R <barcode_list>`
subsets by donor with no re-tagging:

```bash
samtools view -b -R rg_CD_21.txt chr21.bam > CD_21.chr21.bam
```

| Donor | Sex | Dx | chr21 reads | barcodes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CD_21 | M | case | 101,115 | 1,462 |
| CD_31 | F | control | 77,160 | 1,236 |
| CD_36 | M | case | 66,202 | 823 |
| CD_48 | F | control | 95,383 | 1,343 |
| **total** | | | **339,860** | 4,864 |

339,860 of chr21's 629,035 reads (54%) — the remainder belong to the 3,746
barcodes with no donor assignment, which are dropped.

# Per-donor results

| Donor | reads in | events tested | cis | trans | untestable (`nan`) | passing `isolaser_filter` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CD_21 | 95,349 | 169,060 | 25 | 2,423 | 166,434 | **0** |
| CD_31 | 72,586 | 131,704 | 55 | 2,117 | 129,393 | 18 |
| CD_36 | 62,425 | 123,492 | 44 | 1,544 | 121,697 | 11 |
| CD_48 | 89,804 | 146,969 | 31 | 2,357 | 144,412 | 5 |

Two things to take from this:

* **98.5% of events are untestable.** A heterozygous SNP and the splicing event
  must fall on the *same* read, and at ~506 bp median read length with
  62–101 k reads per donor, usually they do not.
* **Per-donor yield is very thin** — CD_21 produced zero events passing the
  filter, the others 5–18.

# Joint results

| | |
|---|---|
| Events testable jointly | 1,936 |
| **cis** | **95** |
| ambiguous | 37 |
| trans | 1,804 |

The joint step recovers more than any single donor (95 vs 25–55), which is the
expected behaviour: it pools depth-normalised haplotype counts across donors
and asks whether the *same allele* associates with the *same* splicing change
in independent individuals.

Coverage is good — of the 95 cis events, **86 have DP ≥ 10 in all four
donors**, and none rest on a single donor:

| Donors with data | Events |
|---|---|
| 4 | 86 |
| 3 | 5 |
| 2 | 4 |
| 1 | 0 |

## But 95 events is not 95 signals

Collapsing by gene and variant:

| | Count |
|---|---|
| Rows | 95 |
| Unique exonic parts | 75 |
| **Unique variants** | **19** |
| **Unique genes** | **7** |

| Gene | Events |
|---|---|
| COL6A1 | 39 |
| IFNAR1 | 30 |
| TTC3 | 10 |
| GET1 | 7 |
| GART | 4 |
| ATP5PF | 4 |
| SPATC1L | 1 |

So chr21 yields **7 genes**. Two of them (COL6A1, IFNAR1) account for 73% of
rows, because one variant is tested against many overlapping exonic parts in
the same gene. **Always collapse by gene or variant before interpreting or
counting.**

## Top events by ΔPSI

| Gene | Variant | Exonic part | ΔPSI | COV |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GART | chr21:33535273 C>T | 33542547–33542586 (−) | 0.539 | 31 |
| TTC3 | chr21:37201716 C>T | 37157160–37157214 (+) | 0.358 | 34 |
| IFNAR1 | chr21:33341122 G>A | 33324903–33324921 (+) | 0.239 | 86 |
| IFNAR1 | chr21:33341116 G>A | 33355865–33355870 (+) | 0.181 | 316 |

The IFNAR1 rows are the better-supported ones: all four donors carry
DP 68–176 with consistent PSI. GART and TTC3 have the largest effects but rest
on COV 31–34, so treat them as provisional.

# Verdict

**The pipeline works.** Split → per donor → `combine_vcf` (GATK) →
`isolaser_joint` runs clean, and the joint step behaves as designed.

**The yield at this depth does not support biology.** 7 genes on chr21, with
per-donor filtered counts of 0–18, is a plumbing result.

# Scaling up

chr21 is ~1.5% of the genome. Genome-wide gives each donor **6.2–9.3 M reads**
instead of 62–101 k — roughly 90× more — which should lift per-donor yields
into a usable range.

With all three timepoints now available, the joint analysis could also run over
**12 samples (4 donors × 3 timepoints)** rather than 4. Alternatively the
timepoints can be pooled per donor to maximise depth, since haplotypes do not
change with stimulation.

## Blocker for the genome-wide run

We only have `chr21.fa`. Going genome-wide needs:

1. the full GRCh38 FASTA (`refdata-gex-GRCh38-2024-A`, ~11 GB), indexed with
   `.fai` and `.dict`
2. the GTF normalisation, transcriptome FASTA and exonic-parts DB rebuilt for
   all contigs

# Notes for reproducing

Several non-obvious things are baked into the scripts:

* **Do not use `samtools fastq`.** 20.5% of reads have `QUAL='*'`, and mixed
  QUAL/no-QUAL input makes it truncate silently — 629,035 reads in, 14,255 out,
  no error. The scripts convert with `awk` and assert the read count matches.
* **`isolaser_extract_exon_parts` does not create its `-o` directory.** `mkdir -p`
  first or it dies in pandas.
* **Keep the `#chrom` header on line 1** of `mi_summary.tab` before bgzip —
  `isolaser_filter` uses `pd.read_csv(..., escapechar='#')` and fails with
  `KeyError: 'label'` if it has been sorted into the body.
* **`PyVCF3` is required but undeclared** — `setup.cfg` has `#PyVCF` commented
  out, so `isolaser_joint` dies on `import vcf` until it is installed.
* **Pass `-n`** — isoLASER spawns 64 processes by default, which the login-node
  watchdog kills. Run under SLURM.
* **`|| true` after `sort | head`** — `set -o pipefail` otherwise turns SIGPIPE
  from `head` into a job failure *after* the analysis has succeeded.
* Results are **not bit-reproducible**; phasing uses k-means with random
  initialisation, so marginal events move between runs.
